requirement: Describe the study as a prospective two-year implementation project in seven Pakro sub-district communities, with a longitudinal cohort and caregiver/community survey components and repeated baseline-to-evaluation comparisons rather than a randomized parallel-arm trial.

evidence.text: The protocol defines a two-year implementation-research longitudinal cohort with prevalence surveys and caregiver questionnaires, comparing baseline and evaluation findings.

requirement: Represent the intervention accurately: test all consenting community members aged at least six months by malaria rapid diagnostic test, treat RDT-confirmed parasitaemia with nationally recommended artemisinin combination therapy, follow treated cases on days 1, 2, 3 and 7, and provide home-based testing and treatment between quarterly MTTT rounds.

evidence.text: The protocol describes community-wide RDT testing, ACT treatment, directly observed follow-up and quarterly rounds with home-based management between rounds.

requirement: Define distinct analysis populations and denominators for the longitudinal child cohort, each cross-sectional community survey, all tested community members, caregiver questionnaires, hospital-record analyses and qualitative interviews; do not call all of them one undifferentiated analysis population.

evidence.text: The protocol describes several nested data sources: a selected child cohort, whole-community testing and treatment, caregiver questionnaires, focus groups and hospital records.

requirement: Define the primary outcome as asymptomatic malaria parasitaemia prevalence measured by RDT among afebrile participants, with afebrile status based on absence of recent fever and measured temperature below 37.5 degrees Celsius, evaluated over time and across intervention communities.

evidence.text: The objectives and data-analysis text define longitudinal malaria prevalence, RDT confirmation and the 37.5 degree distinction for clinical malaria.
The analysis plan identifies asymptomatic parasitaemia as the primary objective for comparison over time and between communities.

requirement: Specify operational derivations for asymptomatic parasitaemia, symptomatic community malaria, hospital-confirmed malaria and febrile illness, including the fever look-back window, temperature rule, RDT positivity, repeat episodes and the denominator for each prevalence or proportion.

evidence.text: The protocol describes RDT testing, treatment and broad symptomatic versus asymptomatic definitions but does not fully operationalize repeat events and all denominators.

requirement: Map every analysis to the intended time structure: baseline, each prevalence survey before subsequent quarterly MTTT rounds, treated-case follow-up on days 1, 2, 3 and 7, monthly implementation monitoring, and the final evaluation within the two-year study.

evidence.text: The protocol provides the two-year framework, repeated pre-intervention surveys, quarterly intervention schedule, treated-case follow-up and monthly monitoring.

requirement: Summarize baseline demographic, clinical and parasitological variables with proportions for categorical variables and means or medians with variability for continuous variables, inspect graphs and outliers, and compare continuous variables using t tests or ANOVA with Wilcoxon or Kruskal-Wallis alternatives and categorical variables using chi-square tests.

evidence.text: The baseline-comparison paragraph specifies descriptive summaries, graphical checks and parametric or nonparametric comparisons by variable type.

requirement: For the primary asymptomatic-parasitaemia analysis, compare time and community/intervention groups using chi-square or Fisher exact tests and logistic or conditional logistic regression, adjusting at least for age, insecticide-treated-net use and baseline temperature; predefine when ordinary versus conditional logistic regression is used.

evidence.text: The primary-objective paragraph names the categorical tests, logistic alternatives and candidate confounders but does not define the selection rule.

requirement: Assess ordered change in asymptomatic parasitaemia prevalence over repeated surveys using a Cochran-Armitage trend test, clearly identifying the ordered survey variable and reporting the direction and uncertainty of the trend.

evidence.text: The primary-objective paragraph calls for a Cochrane Armitage test of trends over time.

requirement: Analyze symptomatic parasitaemia identified in hospital records and in the community separately over time using chi-square or Fisher exact tests and logistic or conditional logistic regression, with endpoint-specific denominators and adjustment variables prespecified.

evidence.text: The secondary-objective paragraph specifies separate hospital and community symptomatic-parasitaemia comparisons with categorical tests and logistic-model alternatives.

requirement: Define anaemia in cohort children as haemoglobin below 10 g/dL, flag severe anaemia below 7 g/dL, and compare anaemia across ordered time and communities using a Cochran-Armitage trend test and chi-square or Fisher exact tests respectively.
acceptable_values: chi-square or Fisher exact across communities

evidence.text: The protocol defines anaemia and severe-anaemia thresholds in cohort children.
The analysis plan specifies trend testing over time and categorical comparison across communities.

requirement: Use binomial logistic regression for the intervention's association with febrile illness, after defining the binary febrile-illness outcome, eligible observation period, within-household or within-person correlation handling and adjustment set.

evidence.text: The final sentence assigns a binomial logistic regression to febrile illness but does not operationalize the outcome or dependence structure.

requirement: Account for the hierarchical and repeated data structure—observations within participants, participants within households and communities, and repeated surveys—using an explicitly justified correlation approach; do not treat all observations as independent without justification.

evidence.text: The protocol defines repeated cohort surveys and links each participant to a household and community.

requirement: State the primary estimand for MTTT impact, including the target population, baseline-to-post-intervention contrast, prevalence variable, survey time, and strategies for migration, loss to follow-up, missed survey rounds, treatment nonreceipt and changing community composition.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the intervention and baseline-to-evaluation intent but does not formalize intercurrent-event handling for this mobile community cohort.

requirement: Predefine missing-data handling for absent survey rounds, missing RDT or temperature results, incomplete questionnaires, unavailable hospital records and attrition from the cohort, including a sensitivity analysis that addresses informative loss or migration.

evidence.text: The protocol anticipates household tracking and follow-up but gives no statistical missing-data or migration procedure.

requirement: Define the inferential hierarchy and multiplicity strategy across repeated timepoints, seven communities, asymptomatic and symptomatic parasitaemia, hospital outcomes, anaemia and febrile illness; if analyses are exploratory, label them and avoid implying one confirmatory familywise claim.
acceptable_values: familywise strategy or explicit no-adjustment rationale

evidence.text: The protocol contains multiple objectives, times, communities and outcomes without an inferential hierarchy or multiplicity rule.
The reference names multiple tests across endpoint families but no error-control strategy.

requirement: Preserve and reconcile the prospective sample-size statements: approximately 4,500 community members, an initial survey calculation of 368 children under 50% prevalence and 5% precision, inflation to 460 for 10% loss and 10% nonresponse, and 116 children in each of four age groups; identify and correct the printed '38/1-0.2' arithmetic typo without substituting the registry's later actual enrollment of 5,000.

evidence.text: The protocol gives the prospective community and cohort targets, assumptions and age-group allocation, with an internally inconsistent printed calculation.

requirement: Define hospital-use outcomes using prespecified numerators, denominators, source registers and calendar windows for malaria consultations, admissions and confirmed malaria cases before versus during/after MTTT; distinguish counts, rates and proportions.

evidence.text: The protocol proposes comparing hospital consultations/admissions and confirmed cases across baseline and evaluation but does not fully reconcile the hospital outcome denominators.

requirement: Specify the cost-benefit perspective, time horizon, currency/year, intervention costs, health-system costs, participant spending, malaria cases prevented and valuation method; the protocol's broad comparison is not by itself an executable economic analysis.

evidence.text: The protocol makes cost-benefit an objective and proposes comparing prior program spending and household malaria spending with MTTT, without a full economic-analysis specification.

requirement: Prespecify analysis of implementation challenges and qualitative questionnaire, focus-group, interview and field-note data, including coding framework, coder roles, theme development, saturation or completeness criteria and integration with quantitative findings.

evidence.text: The protocol makes implementation barriers an objective and specifies questionnaires, focus groups, interviews and field documentation but no qualitative analysis procedure.

requirement: Define the safety population as treated participants or another explicit denominator and summarize adverse effects during days 1, 2, 3 and 7 by ACT regimen, age group, seriousness, severity, relationship, action and outcome, including referral of severe anaemia.

evidence.text: The protocol requires treatment follow-up and adverse-effect documentation and specifies referral for haemoglobin below 7 g/dL, but supplies no safety analysis plan.

requirement: Keep the two-page reference analysis document annotation-only. The model-visible protocol may expose sample-size and a simple chi-square prevalence comparison, but must not be supplemented with the reference-only t-test/ANOVA alternatives, logistic and conditional-logistic models, named confounders or trend tests.

evidence.text: Full-page review found broad protocol design, sample-size and a simple prevalence comparison but not the full independent reference plan.
The independent reference contains the additional endpoint-specific statistical choices and remains under the reference role.
